cited_details.statement: Manifold learning methods are believed to be good at handling nonlinear data and at discovering their intrinsic local geometry in low-dimensional embedding spaces (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0925231222007044).

The same perspective applies directly to image data: many natural image sets are samples of a low-dimensional manifold in the space of all possible images, and understanding this manifold is described as a key first step in image analysis (https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/ipsjtcva/1/0/1_0_83/_article).

The original framework is documented as a global geometric framework for nonlinear dimensionality reduction, and discusses the Isomap method for dimensionality reduction with studies of its performance on both artificial and natural datasets (https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Reduction-A-Global-Geometric-Framework-for-Tenenbaum-Silva/2878f950f0ad19ccec6bab04873895e89f5bece0).

Isomap's global coordinates provide a simple way to analyze and manipulate high-dimensional observations in terms of their intrinsic nonlinear structure (https://pdodds.w3.uvm.edu/files/papers/others/2000/tenenbaum2000a.pdf).

The original LLE paper, titled "Nonlinear dimensionality reduction by locally linear embedding," was authored by Sam Roweis and Lawrence Saul and published in Science, volume 290, number 5500, on December 22, 2000, on pages 2323-2326 (https://cs.nyu.edu/home/people/in_memoriam/roweis/lle/publications.html).

The method performs nonlinear dimensionality reduction through locally linear embedding, as documented in the original publication (https://cs.nyu.edu/home/people/in_memoriam/roweis/lle/publications.html).
Laplacian Eigenmaps is described as a non-linear dimensionality reduction algorithm based on spectral techniques (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U31TIICsHiA).

A PyData Berlin 2018 presentation discusses this spectral method and references the original Laplacian Eigenmaps work, situating the algorithm within the broader literature on spectral methods for dimensionality reduction (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U31TIICsHiA).

The J-Stage survey on manifold learning for images presents natural image sets as samples of a low-dimensional manifold in the space of all possible images, identifying the understanding of this manifold as a key first step in image analysis (https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/ipsjtcva/1/0/1_0_83/_article).

The 2022 work by Han, titled "Enhance explainability of manifold learning," argues that manifold learning is believed to be good at handling nonlinear data and discovering their intrinsic local geometry in low-dimensional embeddings (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0925231222007044).

Furthermore, the Laplacian Eigenmaps entry is a presentation rather than a peer-reviewed publication, so methodological claims drawn from it should be read with that context in mind (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U31TIICsHiA).
